title: The Queen of the Field Mice, part 1
attribution: From The Wonderful Wizard of Oz by L. Frank Baum (1900), via Project Gutenberg, in reading order.
body: “We cannot be far from the road of yellow brick, now,” remarked the Scarecrow, as he stood beside the girl, “for we have come nearly as far as the river carried us away.”

The Tin Woodman was about to reply when he heard a low growl, and turning his head (which worked beautifully on hinges) he saw a strange beast come bounding over the grass toward them. It was, indeed, a great yellow Wildcat, and the Woodman thought it must be chasing something, for its ears were lying close to its head and its mouth was wide open, showing two rows of ugly teeth, while its red eyes glowed like balls of fire. As it came nearer the Tin Woodman saw that running before the beast was a little gray field mouse, and although he had no heart he knew it was wrong for the Wildcat to try to kill such a pretty, harmless creature.
So the Woodman raised his axe, and as the Wildcat ran by he gave it a quick blow that cut the beast’s head clean off from its body, and it rolled over at his feet in two pieces.
The field mouse, now that it was freed from its enemy, stopped short; and coming slowly up to the Woodman it said, in a squeaky little voice:
“Oh, thank you! Thank you ever so much for saving my life.”
“Don’t speak of it, I beg of you,” replied the Woodman. “I have no heart, you know, so I am careful to help all those who may need a friend, even if it happens to be only a mouse.”
“Only a mouse!” cried the little animal, indignantly. “Why, I am a Queen—the Queen of all the Field Mice!”
“Oh, indeed,” said the Woodman, making a bow.
“Therefore you have done a great deed, as well as a brave one, in saving my life,” added the Queen.
At that moment several mice were seen running up as fast as their little legs could carry them, and when they saw their Queen they exclaimed:

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what beast came bounding over the grass?
options: A great yellow Wildcat
A gray wolf from the forest
One of the Kalidahs
A field mouse the size of a cat

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what was the Wildcat chasing?
options: A little gray field mouse
A brightly coloured bird
The Cowardly Lion
Toto, across the grass

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did the Tin Woodman stop the Wildcat?
options: He cut its head off with one blow of his axe
He caught it by the tail as it ran past
He frightened it away by banging his tin chest
He stood in its path until it turned aside

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did the mouse turn out to be?
options: The Queen of all the Field Mice
The oldest mouse in the meadow
A servant of the Wicked Witch
A messenger from the Emerald City

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did the Wildcat look as it ran?
options: Ears flat, mouth open, eyes glowing red
Ears pricked, mouth shut, eyes half closed
Head down, tail high, moving slowly
Limping, as though it had been hurt

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why did the Tin Woodman act although he has no heart?
options: He knew the killing was wrong even without one
The Scarecrow told him what he ought to do
He hoped the mouse would reward him for it
He had been attacked by the Wildcat himself

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Woodman say about helping others?
options: Having no heart, he takes care to help anyone in need
He helps only those who can repay the favour
He helps because the Scarecrow expects it of him
He would rather not be thanked by an animal

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Queen object to the Woodman's words?
options: He had called her only a mouse
He had refused her thanks outright
He had bowed too low before her
He had killed the Wildcat too quickly

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does indignantly convey?
options: With offended dignity
With great gratitude
With sudden fear
With quiet amusement

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the passage?
options: A small act of mercy turns out to have saved a queen
A wildcat attacks the party and is driven off
The travellers find the yellow road again at last
The Tin Woodman regrets killing a living creature

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Scarecrow say about their position?
options: That they could not be far from the yellow road
That they had walked past the road already
That the river had carried them further than he thought
That they should turn back towards the forest

questions.prompt: Per the passage, how did the Tin Woodman's head turn?
options: Beautifully, on hinges
Stiffly, needing oil
Not at all, being rusted
Only with the Scarecrow's help

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the mouse do once it was free?
options: Stopped short and came slowly up to the Woodman
Ran straight on into the long grass
Climbed onto the Woodman's tin foot
Called at once for the other mice

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what did the Woodman think the Wildcat was doing?
options: Chasing something, from the way it ran
Hunting the party themselves
Fleeing from a larger beast
Guarding the road to the river

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, how does the Woodman receive the news of the Queen's rank?
options: He makes her a bow
He laughs at the idea
He refuses to believe it
He asks her to prove it

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does harmless describe about the mouse?
options: That it could do no injury to anyone
That it was too small to be seen
That it had no home to run to
That it was already badly hurt

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarises the passage?
options: A rescue by the roadside earns the party a powerful friend
A battle with a wildcat costs the Tin Woodman his axe
A mouse leads the travellers back to the yellow road
The Tin Woodman proves he has a heart after all
